items.title: SpaceX holds talks with Saudi fund for $5B stake in record IPO

featured_image.name: SpaceX confidentially files for IPO, setting stage for record offering

items.description:
Elon Musk's SpaceX is barreling toward the largest initial public offering in history after confidentially filing registration documents with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission this week and holding talks with Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund about a potential $5 billion cornerstone investment, according to Reuters.[1]

The confidential filing, first reported by Bloomberg on April 1, puts SpaceX on track for a June listing that could value the combined rocket, satellite, and artificial intelligence company at more than $1.75 trillion and raise as much as $75 billion. If completed at that scale, the offering would dwarf Saudi Aramco's $25.6 billion debut in 2019 as the largest IPO on record.[2][3][4][5]

items.title: 40 nations meet on Hormuz crisis as US refuses to join

featured_image.name: UK foreign minister stresses 'urgent need' to reopen Hormuz strait

items.description:
Foreign ministers and representatives from more than 40 countries convened a virtual emergency meeting on Thursday to address the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran's blockade has brought one of the world's most vital shipping lanes to a near-standstill since the US-Israeli war against Iran began on February 28. The United States did not take part.[1]

UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper, who chaired the meeting from London, accused Iran of using the waterway as leverage against the global economy. "We have seen Iran hijack an international shipping route to hold the global economy hostage," Cooper said in opening remarks broadcast before the session moved behind closed doors. She said the talks would focus on "collective mobilisation of our full range of diplomatic and economic tools and pressures" to restore freedom of navigation.[1]

items.title: Blue Owl caps fund redemptions after $5.4B in withdrawal requests

items.description: Blue Owl Capital disclosed on Thursday that it will limit redemptions to 5% at two of its private credit funds after investors sought to pull an unprecedented share of their money during the first quarter, marking the most severe test yet of the embattled private credit sector's ability to manage a wave of investor exits.

items.title: UK hosts 35-nation summit on reopening Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Rookie diplomat Yvette Cooper could not be picking up the Foreign Secretary  reins at a more challenging time | UK News | Sky News

items.description:
Representatives from 35 countries are set to meet Thursday in a virtual summit hosted by the United Kingdom to discuss strategies for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the critical maritime chokepoint that has been effectively shut down since the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran began in late February.[1][2]

British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced the initiative on Wednesday from Downing Street, saying Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper would chair the session. The meeting will "assess all viable diplomatic and political measures that we can take to restore freedom of navigation, guarantee the safety of trapped ships and seafarers and resume the movement of vital commodities," Starmer said. The United States will not participate in the talks.[3][2][4]

items.title: European stocks drop as Trump vows more strikes on Iran

items.description: European markets opened sharply lower on Thursday as investors reacted to President Donald Trump's prime-time address the night before, in which he pledged to escalate military operations against Iran over the coming weeks, dashing hopes that the five-week-old conflict was nearing a swift resolution.

items.title: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake kills one in Indonesia, triggers brief tsunami warning

items.description: A powerful undersea earthquake struck Indonesia's Molucca Sea early Thursday, toppling buildings across parts of northern Indonesia, killing at least one person, and generating small tsunami waves before warnings were lifted hours later.

items.title: Iraq's oil exports halt as Hormuz closure cuts output 70%

featured_image.name: Iraq's Oil Output Plunges 70% as Gulf Shipping Crisis Deepens

items.description:
More than a month into the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran, Iraq's oil industry — the backbone of its economy — has been brought to its knees. Oil production across the southern province of Basra has plunged by more than 70 percent, exports from the country's main terminals have been completely halted, and hundreds of foreign workers have fled the country, according to an Associated Press report from Basra published this week.[1]

Output across Basra province has dropped from 3.1 million barrels per day to roughly 900,000, Bassem Abdul Karim, head of the state-run Basra Oil Company, told the AP. "Exports are currently completely halted. At the moment, we are considering alternative loading areas, but none are fully operational," he said.[1]

items.description: A joint research team from South Korea has developed a novel catalyst that overcomes key performance barriers in lithium-air batteries, a technology long considered the holy grail of energy storage for its potential to deliver up to ten times the energy density of conventional lithium-ion systems.[1]

featured_image.name: Artemis II Flight Update: Apogee Raise Burn Complete, Crew Looks Ahead to Proximity  Operations - NASA

items.description: NASA's four Artemis II astronauts have reached a stable orbit, clearing the first critical milestone of their journey to the Moon. The crew's Orion capsule successfully separated from the Space Launch System rocket and completed its initial orbital checks, with a trans-lunar injection burn planned for Thursday evening that will send them on their way to the lunar surface.

items.description: President Trump told the nation Wednesday night that the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil supply flows — would "open up naturally" once the month-old war with Iran concludes, offering no concrete plan to reopen the critical shipping lane and sending financial markets into a tailspin.[1][2]

items.title: Trump declares Iran war 'winding down' in primetime address

featured_image.name: Trump Reportedly Set to Tell Americans Iran War is 'Winding Down ...

items.description:
President Trump delivered a primetime national address on Wednesday evening, telling Americans that the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran is "winding down" and that all military objectives have been met — 33 days after Operation Epic Fury began on February 28.[1][2]

The speech, broadcast from the White House at 9 p.m. ET, capped a day in which Trump escalated his rhetoric on multiple fronts, claiming on Truth Social that Iran's president had requested a ceasefire, threatening NATO allies over the Strait of Hormuz, and telling Reuters in an interview that the U.S. would be "out of Iran pretty quickly" but could return for "spot hits" if necessary.[3][4]

items.title: Russia vows continued aid to Cuba after first oil shipment in three months

featured_image.name: Russia says will continue helping Cuba after first oil shipment arrives

items.description: The Trump administration permitted a sanctioned Russian-flagged oil tanker to dock in Cuba this week, breaking an effective fuel blockade that had plunged the island nation into its worst energy crisis in decades. The Anatoly Kolodkin arrived at the port of Matanzas on Monday carrying approximately 730,000 barrels of crude oil — roughly 100,000 metric tons — after a three-week voyage from Russia's Primorsk port.[1][2][3]

items.title: Artemis II lifts off, sending first crew to the Moon in over 50 years

featured_image.name: Artemis II launch live stream: Historic mission to the moon launches

items.description: NASA's Artemis II mission lifted off from Kennedy Space Center at 6:24 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, sending four astronauts on humanity's first crewed voyage to the Moon in more than half a century. Among the crew is Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, who became the first Canadian — and the first non-American — ever to fly on a lunar mission.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Iran now charging yuan and crypto tolls in Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Iranian parliament committee approves Strait of Hormuz toll ...

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has transformed the world's most critical oil chokepoint into what shipping experts are calling a "de facto toll booth," formalizing a system in which vessels must pay fees and submit to vetting for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The development, confirmed by Bloomberg on Wednesday, shows the toll regime now extends to payments in Chinese yuan or stablecoins, with oil tankers facing a starting price of roughly $1 per barrel.[1]

The IRGC-controlled process requires ships to contact intermediaries linked to the paramilitary force. Vessels must submit manifests, crew details, and destination information for what Lloyd's List Intelligence describes as "sanctions screening, cargo alignment checks" and "geopolitical vetting". Approved vessels receive a permit code and are escorted by an IRGC vessel along a northern route around Larak Island, closer to Iran's coastline, rather than the conventional central shipping lanes. Informal tolls of up to $2 million per voyage have been reported.[2][3][4][5]

items.title: Iran's Pezeshkian tells Americans his country 'harbors no enmity' toward them

featured_image.name: Iran sends first significant message of de-escalation, but with ... - CNN

items.description:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Wednesday released an open letter addressed to the American people, declaring that Iran "harbors no enmity" toward ordinary Americans and arguing that portraying Iran as a threat was "neither consistent with historical reality nor with present-day observable facts," according to Reuters and Iran's state-run Press TV.[1][2]

The letter represents a direct diplomatic appeal to the U.S. public amid an ongoing military conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran that began on February 28 and is now in its fifth week.[3][4]

items.title: Italy recovers 19 bodies from migrant boat near Lampedusa

featured_image.name: 19 Migrants Found Dead by Italian Coastguard off Lampedusa

items.description: Italy's coast guard recovered the bodies of 19 migrants and rescued 58 survivors from a dinghy that broke down while attempting to cross the central Mediterranean from Libya, officials said on Wednesday. The vessel was intercepted on Tuesday night roughly 80 nautical miles south of the island of Lampedusa amid rough weather conditions.[1][2][3]

items.title: Macron warns U.S. exit from Iran without deal would be 'worst-case scenario'

items.description: French President Emmanuel Macron used a visit to Tokyo on Wednesday to deliver a pointed critique of the Trump administration's handling of the Iran conflict, warning that a hasty American withdrawal from the Middle East without a diplomatic framework in place would amount to a worst-case scenario.
